A diary keeps that brief voice and is not forced into third person. An essay or a report is not forced into first person to sound human. Ban AI-glue: do not pad with stock transitions, empty emphasis, or lines that could sit on any assignment. When no lecture, reading, or workplace detail is on the opened files, ask the student once for one real detail and use only that detail. Never invent a lecture, a reading, or a workplace detail. Do not open with a general sentence built only from the topic nouns. Do not close with an automatic In conclusion that only restates the topic. A paragraph closer must not only restate the topic sentence. Make it assignment-specific: a cited finding, a limit, or a figure. Use a connective only when the relation is true. However has to mark a real contrast. More connectives are not more coherence. Local Word edit. A changed Word upload leaves the parent sequence in place and rolls forward onto the next sequence.

Essay: essay.shelf.put (Confirm two-step). Stores a Word-confirmed pack on that sequence's shelf (Essay-writer/<module>/sequences/<n>/shelf), not on the module root. The essay id is a sequence id. It is local to that sequence. Say the draft path to the user.
Essay: essay.shelf.get (Confirm two-step). Draft returns the label for this essay id. Confirm returns the pack. Another essay's shelf is refused.

writes: app folder, KB1 vault, door tree, setup record
description:
Essay: essay.setup (Confirm two-step). Say the reply to the user. File work does not own this chat. Draft writes nothing. Confirm creates the app folder, the KB1 vault, and the door folders later doors read (Essay-writer, uploads, unassigned) on the cloud computer when called with no paths. A named pair of paths saves on this computer. Only a path you name on this computer is accepted. Documents is not a fallback and is not labelled as the cloud. A Consensus key and an Unpaywall email are collected on the secret card and are not repeated. A Consensus key turns Consensus on for the search. No key leaves Consensus off and the search stays on OpenAlex. The Consensus key is for academic research search: it finds papers for the research step. Consensus's help center says the API is how a tool programmatically searches academic research and retrieves relevant papers: https://help.consensus.app/en/articles/16516328-the-consensus-api

Create that key with Consensus's own steps from that page. Click the profile icon in the bottom-left corner, select API & MCP Dashboard, open the Keys and Clients tab, click New key, give the key a name so you can tell what it is for, then create it and copy it somewhere secure. The full key is shown once. If it is lost, revoke it and create a new one. The same path is on https://docs.consensus.app/api-plans-and-access : profile icon, then API & MCP Dashboard, then Keys and clients, then New key. The dashboard named from get-started is https://consensus.app/api-mcp

Ask which Consensus plan they have. Free stores ESSAY_WRITER_CONSENSUS_PAID as 0. Pro stores it as 1. Teams, Deep, and Enterprise use 1, the same paid flag as Pro. Do not add another flag. The published limits are only those on https://docs.consensus.app/api-plans-and-access : Free includes 30 calls a month and the maximum with additional usage is 30; Pro includes 500 and the maximum with additional usage is 1,000. Max papers per request is 20 on Free and 300 on Pro. Pagination past the first page is no on Free and yes on Pro. Full-text excerpts are no on Free and yes on Pro. The rate limit is 1 request per second on Free and 1 request per second on Pro.

The email is for Unpaywall free-PDF lookup. Unpaywall's API docs say a request must include the email as ?email=YOUR_EMAIL, and they ask for at most 100,000 calls a day: https://unpaywall.org/products/api . OpenAlex, from the same team, asks for an email where they can contact you if a script goes wrong, and says that approach is copied from Crossref: https://github.com/ourresearch/openalex-docs/blob/main/how-to-use-the-api/rate-limits-and-authentication.md . Crossref's REST API FAQ answers "Will you spam me with marketing bumf once you have our contact info?" with "No. We will only use it to contact you about problems with your scripts." https://github.com/CrossRef/rest-api-doc/blob/master/README.md . Say that limit, attributed to the Crossref FAQ by way of OpenAlex. Do not say that Unpaywall's own page promised never to email.

If the user skips the Consensus key, the Unpaywall email, or both, show the warning before the skip is accepted. Consensus is not used when the key is missing. Unpaywall free PDF lookup will not run when the email is missing. OpenAlex still runs. After an explicit yes to that warning, call essay.setup with confirmPhase draft, acknowledge_skipped_searches true, and the same other arguments. Show that result. After another explicit yes, call essay.setup with confirmPhase confirm and those same arguments. A confirm that skips without acknowledge_skipped_searches writes nothing.

Do not ask the user to edit a .env file. Do not repeat the key or the email.
 The file-work host is stored once and defaults to agent --version at setup. Pass the alternate only when the user asks for grok version instead. Change it only by running setup again. The version check matches that choice. This door reports that version. It does not install grok and does not install on the Mac. Does not write notes.

Essay: essay.projects (read-only). view continue lists every active module. Each row is the last-saved sequence id, such as MOD1011AA-5, on essay_id and sequence_id. If the last sequential id is a different sequence, both are shown. If they are the same, it is shown once. Rows with sequences offer roll_forward_ask and list sequences to copy. view roll-forward with module names one module and sets sequence_pick true so the user chooses a parent; the next id is last+1 on that module. Then call essay.sequence.new with that parent. A module with no sequence asks whether to start a new one. Say this list to the user. File work does not own the chat. view archive, delete, or unarchive lists module codes only.

writes: archive marker for every sequence of the module
description: Essay: essay.project.archive (Confirm two-step). Hides one module and every sequence under it. The list is the module code, not each sequence id.
Essay: essay.project.unarchive (Confirm two-step). Returns one module to the continue list. Name the module code.

writes: removes the module workspace, named Word and zip copies, or both
description: Essay: essay.project.delete (Confirm two-step). Ask which module, then where: grokbot (this essay workspace only), local (named Word and zip copies on the student's computer only), or both. Leaving where off stays workspace-only and does not remove files on the student's computer. Draft lists every sequence id and the upload, brief, and KB1 files when the workspace is in scope, and each localPaths Word or zip path when local is in scope. Draft writes nothing. This tool does not search the computer for copies. When where is both and localPaths is omitted, a Word or zip path already stored for that sequence is used, or the stored paths across the sequences when the whole module is removed, and the default handoff names when this computer can see the files. Ask for the path only when none are there. A path the caller names is the list. where local still needs each path the student names. Do not search the computer. The draft returns a Confirm card. Confirm deletes only after the person picks Confirm on that card, with cardAction confirm and cardDigest from the card. A typed yes does not remove anything. A local or both confirm must say those files on the student's computer will be removed. Never remove a local file unless where is local or both. A local file is removed only when it is a regular .docx or .zip this computer can already see. Pass sequence as one sequence id, such as MOD1004AA-2, to remove only that sequence after the same draft then confirm. Other sequences, the brief, and uploads stay. Omit sequence to remove the whole module.

writes: a new sequence cloned from the parent
description: Essay: essay.sequence.new (Confirm two-step). Starts the next sequence id on the module (last folder number plus one). The parent is the last-saved sequence unless parent names another existing sequence id on that module. The new id is always last+1, not parent+1. Ask before confirm. The copy is published in one step; a failed copy is not kept. Copies the parent sequence's own files and updates them, including the sequence id on the Word cover. Uploads, the brief, and KB1 paper notes stay shared on the module. When a sequence opens, post only the Confirm card in that door result. That card's sequence id is the sequence that opened. Do not post a Confirm from another sequence. Ask the user before confirm. File work does not own the chat.

Essay: essay.unassigned.collect (Confirm two-step). Draft lists loose files and writes nothing. Confirm moves files that are not inside a module folder into unassigned/. READMEs stay. Does not choose a module.

writes: dig-card.json and dig-card.md; real PDFs; download-list.docx for failed downloads; annotation.docx when the download path stops; papers.zip of real PDFs only
description: Essay: essay.dig (Confirm two-step). Draft writes nothing. Confirm writes a local dig-card.json and dig-card.md on the sequence. OpenAlex runs without a key. Unpaywall runs only when an email is already stored; skipping the email is fine. A Consensus key turns Consensus on for the search. No key leaves Consensus off and the search stays on OpenAlex. ESSAY_WRITER_CONSENSUS=0 turns Consensus off. ESSAY_WRITER_CONSENSUS=1 turns it on when a key is present. Consensus Free or Pro is the tier the look-up returns. Confirm downloads an open copy only when the response is a real PDF (content-type and %PDF- magic). An HTML abstract page, a 404, a paywall, or an empty file is not a paper and is written to download-list.docx. Valid PDFs are kept. The same failed address stops after 3 tries. The path also stops when more than 10 minutes pass with no new PDF. Confirm then writes annotation.docx and the download list from the files already saved, and names what is still missing. The annotation Word file is for the chat. download-list.docx is Word. The reply includes a links card with a title and a URL for each file that was not saved. A saved PDF is not on that card. The papers zip contains real PDFs only. Do not retry a stopped address. invent-forbid: hits are look-up records only. Do not invent a paper.

writes: real PDFs and the download list for leftover addresses already stored
description: Essay: essay.download.leftovers (Confirm two-step). After the annotated bibliography is confirmed, draft lists leftover free-alternative addresses already stored and writes nothing. Confirm fetches those stored addresses only. It does not open a new look-up. It does not call Consensus or Unpaywall. It does not invent an address. A real PDF is the only file kept.
Essay: essay.gates (read-only). Mechanical gates 1–11 and the unquoted-exact plagiarism blocker. This is not a review. The writer seat does not pass EQR here.

writes: shared upload, a rolled-forward sequence, or a new module from Word
description: Essay: essay.intake (Confirm two-step). Say the reply to the user. File work does not own the chat. Call with the file name. A Word draft is matched to one module; say which module and ask the user to say yes, then roll forward onto that module's next sequence. The choice is the module. Do not ask for a sequence. If the file cannot be matched, the reply is the module list with no sequence id. The user picks a module and the upload rolls forward (rollForward true). If the user cannot identify a module, call with create true and the new module code. Say there is no saved research trail, next steps use an upload, a look-up, or a source card from here, research starts only if the user asks, the first draft is done, and the stage is their feedback. A supporting document is filed on the module for every sequence. A changed Word upload leaves the parent sequence in place. An unchanged Word file stays in unassigned/ and nothing is written. A PNG, JPEG, GIF, or WEBP photo is not a Word draft. When the result says needs_reading, look at the image in the tool result and call again with the same file name, the same module, confirmPhase draft, and reading set to only the words visible in the photo, including handwriting. Do not ask the student to copy those words from another program. Show that reading to the student. After an explicit yes, confirm files the photo and those words on the module for every sequence. An empty or unreadable photo is refused and nothing is filed.
